--- title: "ASM Chapter 6" author: "Dr Alun ap Rhisiart" date: "2026-10-28" categories: [code, julia, statistics, asm, ecology] execute: echo: true warning: false output: true engine: julia draft: true --- Chapter 6 of Applied Statistical Modelling for Ecologists, by Marc Kéry and Kenneth Kellner, considers the case of two predictors in a linear regression model. Traditionally this would be a t-test, comparing two means across groups defined by one categorical predictor, but here we extend it to include an additional continuous predictor. ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using RCall, DataFrames R""" set.seed(61) n1 <- 60 n2 <- 40 μ1 <- 105.0 μ2 <- 77.5 σ <- 2.75 n <- n1 + n2 y1 <- rnorm(n1, μ1, σ) y2 <- rnorm(n2, μ2, σ) y <- c(y1, y2) x<- rep(c(0, 1), c(n1, n2)) """ x = @rget x y = @rget y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 100-element Vector{Float64}: 103.95326953068289 103.96894538093773 100.26704205115483 105.96381428271559 101.19383476476229 104.48206409409144 106.93496962303902 106.41307207477664 108.77833408034238 104.12810562499166 ⋮ 81.25986177508724 79.75148317107431 73.91994818909625 78.76875528208912 78.51005049070446 73.19727114861206 76.3968109937144 77.0066184709535 78.43830073306984 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using GLM y_obs = DataFrame(y = y, x = x) model = lm(@formula(y ~ x), y_obs) model ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` StatsModels.TableRegressionModel{LinearModel{GLM.LmResp{Vector{Float64}}, GLM.DensePredChol{Float64, LinearAlgebra.CholeskyPivoted{Float64, Matrix{Float64}, Vector{Int64}}}}, Matrix{Float64}} y ~ 1 + x Coefficients: ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Coef. Std. Error t Pr(>|t|) Lower 95% Upper 95% ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── (Intercept) 104.771 0.357902 292.74 <1e-99 104.06 105.481 x -27.6184 0.565893 -48.80 <1e-69 -28.7414 -26.4954 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ``` ::: ::: ::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using HypothesisTests t_test_result = EqualVarianceTTest(y_obs.y[x .== 1], y_obs.y[x .== 0]) t_test_result ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Two sample t-test (equal variance) ---------------------------------- Population details: parameter of interest: Mean difference value under h_0: 0 point estimate: -27.6184 95% confidence interval: (-28.74, -26.5) Test summary: outcome with 95% confidence: reject h_0 two-sided p-value: <1e-69 Details: number of observations: [40,60] t-statistic: -48.8049 degrees of freedom: 98 empirical standard error: 0.565893 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Turing, FlexiChains, MCMCDiagnosticTools @model function linear_model(y, x) α ~ Normal(0, 100) β ~ Normal(0, 100) σ ~ Uniform(1, 10) μ = @. α + β * x y ~ product_distribution(Normal.(μ, σ)) end model_turing = linear_model(y_obs.y, y_obs.x) chains = sample(model_turing, NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 4) summarystats(chains) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}
